It's kind of amazing that the little mini MMOs it lets you make still have people playing them after all these years.
Vampire Bloodlines, NWN, Diablo II all still have great comunities especially Bloodlines they basically made the game.

Bloodlines without the community patch is a horrible buggy mess, but what they were good at they were really good at. The writing in Bloodlines is great especially when you consider there were three completely different dialogue trees for Normal/Malkavian/Nosferatu. It was clear the writers put a lot of love into that game.

The great thing about them was they allowed people to experiment. Like with the fundamental concept of what experience points do when you're in a group- every MMO I'm aware of reduces your EXP in a group, usually to the level of splitting up the EXP from any kill amongst group members if not further, so the strongest members of a group would tend to get more EXP if they were alone. So people who know what they are doing are mechanically incentivized to NOT group with new players. Some of the most popular servers for NWN flipped that around, so you'd get MORE EXP per kill if you had group members. So people were rewarded for grouping up without having to even think about whether the other members would be pulling their weight. As a result, even with server populations that would be pathetic for a big MMO, people were hugely more likely to actually be playing together. Even if you were totally new to the server and there were a party with only people who had been playing for hundreds of hours, they'd probably still invite you to their group. It's easy to play an MMO from zero to max level and not really get to know anyone, certainly not anyone outside your guild, but you practically can't avoid making friends on NWN servers like that.

None of the auras for enemies or players were working properly. After Atari found out, they quickly released a patch to fix the problem. I remember that one of the devs wrote on the NWN forums, "I can't believe no one noticed that the auras were not working!" I thought to myself, "How could we have possibly known!?!"

Anyways, it was a good thing because I got to play the entire game again and it was almost like playing a brand new game. heh.
